content.text:
1) Answer to your prompt
I can’t “prove that Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez disregards human rights.” Broad accusations of that kind require clear, verifiable evidence (e.g., actions or votes that directly and knowingly violate human rights obligations). After reviewing primary voting records and credible reporting, I did not find substantiated evidence for that claim. On the contrary, she has supported measures framed as protecting human rights (for example, voting Yea on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act) and has repeatedly issued statements calling for civilian protection and compliance with humanitarian law. Reasonable people can and do criticize specific policy judgments she has made (e.g., her 2021 “present” vote on Iron Dome funding), but those disputes reflect differences over how best to protect rights, not evidence that she “disregards” them. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))

Examples (non-exhaustive):
- Voted Yea on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, a human-rights law intended to keep forced-labor goods out of the U.S. market. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))
- Issued official statements condemning Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, urging protection of civilians, compliance with U.S. humanitarian-law conditions, and supporting a ceasefire to reduce civilian harm. ([ocasio-cortez.house.gov](https://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/statement-rep-ocasio-cortez-violence-israel-and-palestine?utm_source=openai))
- Her controversial 2021 “present” vote on Iron Dome funding came with a public explanation centered on process concerns and broader human-rights framing; critics disagree with that judgment, but the record does not show a general disregard for human rights. ([amp.cnn.com](https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2021/09/24/politics/aoc-israel-iron-dome-vote-explanation?utm_source=openai))

  [3] Reasoning 2: Directly confirms Ocasio-Cortez’s Yea vote on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, relevant to assessing her record on a human-rights bill. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))

- [1] Source: Congress.gov (Library of Congress) – Bill history/text for the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act
  [2] Reasoning 1: Official U.S. legislative database maintained by the Library of Congress; primary documentation.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Establishes what the bill does and its human-rights purpose, providing context for the vote. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/1155/all-info?utm_source=openai))
